critical_pain_points.title: Fails WCAG AA contrast: "RUРусский"
critical_pain_points.summary: "RUРусский" does not meet the contrast the guidelines require. Its rendered contrast is 1.03:1 against a WCAG AA minimum of 3:1, measured on the page as drawn (text against its own background). A persona could not read it at all after their own eyesight was applied to the capture: too little contrast to make anything out.
critical_pain_points.recommendation: Measured on the pixels: the darker side sits at 0.9216 relative luminance and has to reach 0.2824 or below against a background at 0.9473. #909090 is a neutral that gets there -- any colour at or below that luminance does. This is measured on what the browser actually drew, so checking the declared CSS colours is not enough -- an overlay, a gradient or an image behind the text will not show up there.

critical_pain_points.title: Promised more than it did: Pricing
critical_pain_points.summary: Before touching it they said what they expected: "I expect to see pricing details for GitHub Enterprise Cloud." What arrived was not that -- "The pricing plans page did not appear; the view remains on the main page with generic navigation and content." They tried it 3 times. It cost 0.48 on a 0-1 patience scale -- about a third of the way from calm to walking away, measured across the run rather than assumed.
critical_pain_points.recommendation: Make “Pricing” show what it promises. Right now the click produces nothing a visitor can see, and the label is the thing telling them it should.

alternatives.proposedChange: Reword “Pricing” so a visitor no longer expects to be told something -- right now nothing does. Kept as the fallback, not the recommendation: it treats the symptom rather than the control, and a visitor who reads the new wording correctly still gets nothing for the click.
alternatives.rationale: The half of the either/or not committed to above.

critical_pain_points.evidence: 3 unmet expectations across 1 run and 1 person, costing 0.48 on a 0-1 patience scale -- about a third of the way from calm to walking away
critical_pain_points.observation: The pricing plans page did not appear; the view remains on the main page with generic navigation and content
critical_pain_points.rootCause: The wording is what set the expectation. Reading “Pricing”, this visitor expected to be told something, and got nothing they could see. A control named for what you will get owes you that, or a visible reason you are not getting it. Silence reads as a control that is broken rather than one that declined. They came back to it 3 times, which is what people do when they are sure they used the right control and assume they mis-clicked. This rests on a general web convention, not something this run measured: a control labelled with what it reveals is read as the thing that reveals it, on most sites a visitor has already used.

persona_narration.mentalModel: Across the run, this persona no single pattern -- their expectations of controls varied about as much as the controls did. That model never held against what the page actually did.

limitations: Findings are JourneyTest's own evidence-grounded verdict (blockers/uxFindings/suggestedImprovements/failed pass-criteria) from a real browser run against the target URL, not text inferred from the task description.

Findings tagged source=eyeson-vision-synthesis are cross-persona-aggregated (spec.md section 20/21 cohort/root-cause aggregation): a real vision-model critique of actual JourneyTest screenshots, grounded against a small curated UX-heuristics corpus, then synthesized across every persona that hit the same underlying issue -- never a single persona's individual citation, even when only one persona ran.

Persona quotes are the person's own account of the page, recorded by the persona director as it browsed: what they expected a control to do before they touched it (`persona.expectation`), what actually arrived and how it differed (`persona.reflection`), and how that left them (`persona.affect`, worded from the gap rather than declared). They are first-person statements about a page. They are not the model's completion tokens, which are its own working about refs and evidence capture and are kept out of the report's quotes for exactly that reason.

This run's model calls used temperature > 0 (personaActor.js's acting/reflection calls, 0.7); re-running the same profile against the same page will not reproduce this run's persona quotes word for word. What is reproducible is the persona's disposition -- the compiled behavior and ability profile a re-run is given -- not its exact phrasing.
